lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Could your body ever evolve to hold its breath like a *seal*?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The surprise is that, somewhere on Earth, it has *already* happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most of us come up for air within about a minute, and think that is our *limit*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But your body hides an old diving trick, and it starts in your *chest*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: While you hold your breath, the oxygen in your blood slowly *runs down*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So your body switches on its dive reflex: your heart slows, and blood leaves your hands and *feet*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then your spleen, a small organ under your ribs, squeezes like a *sponge*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It pushes spare red blood cells, which carry oxygen, into your blood like a *backup tank*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Seals have enormous spleens for exactly this *reason*.
